tasks.title: build_submission_package assembles platform-shaped Markdown package
acceptance_criteria: build_submission_package(finding, poc, live_report) returns a single Markdown string with all nine sections present and in template order.
Title, CWE, Severity, Vulnerable Code References, Attack Scenario, Impact and Suggested Fix are sourced from the finding dict.
The PoC Reference section is sourced from the poc dict and the Live-Test Evidence section from the live_report dict.
Missing keys in any input dict degrade gracefully to a clear placeholder rather than raising.

spec.objective: Extend the existing report build into a platform-shaped submission package by mapping the finding, poc, and live_report dicts onto the submission report template and rendering the complete Markdown document.
functional_requirements: Expose build_submission_package(finding: dict, poc: dict, live_report: dict) -> str returning the rendered Markdown submission package.
Populate the Title, CWE, and Severity sections from the finding dict.
Populate the Vulnerable Code References and Attack Scenario sections from the finding dict, rendering code references in a readable list/code-block form.
Populate the PoC Reference section from the poc dict (e.g. script path, command, expected output / artifact reference).
Populate the Live-Test Evidence section from the live_report dict (e.g. observed result, status, captured output).
Populate the Impact and Suggested Fix sections from the finding dict, then assemble all nine sections in the canonical template order via the template loader/renderer.
spec.interfaces: build_submission_package(finding: dict, poc: dict, live_report: dict) -> str
edge_cases: One or more of finding/poc/live_report is empty or has missing keys (must yield placeholder markers, not exceptions).
Vulnerable code references provided as a list versus a single string.
Severity provided as a CVSS-style dict versus a plain label string.
Multiline PoC commands or evidence output that must remain valid Markdown inside code fences.
non_goals: Do not POST or otherwise submit the package to huntr or any bounty platform.
Do not perform live testing or PoC execution here; consume the already-produced live_report and poc dicts.
spec.implementation_notes:
Build on load_submission_template/render_template from the loader task. Reuse field naming conventions already present in ngv2/submission.py, ngv2/report.py, and ngv2/contracts.py where they overlap (title, cwe, severity, impact, fix) rather than inventing new keys. Keep all nine required sections: title, CWE, severity, vulnerable code refs, attack scenario, PoC reference, live-test evidence, impact, suggested fix.

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Representative finding dict (title, cwe, severity, code_refs, attack_scenario, impact, fix), a poc dict (script/command/output), and a live_report dict (status/observed/output); plus minimal/empty variants for graceful-degradation cases.

token_budget_ratio.note: Core deliverable; section mapping is straightforward but breadth of inputs warrants heavier test coverage.

tasks.title: Submission report template loader and field renderer
acceptance_criteria: load_submission_template(path=None) returns the contents of the submission report template, defaulting to the legacy template path.

When the template file is missing or unreadable, a built-in default template string is returned that contains all nine required section headers (Title, CWE, Severity, Vulnerable Code References, Attack Scenario, PoC Reference, Live-Test Evidence, Impact, Suggested Fix).
render_template(template, fields) substitutes named placeholders and emits a clear marker for any field that is absent.

spec.objective: Provide the template-loading and field-rendering substrate that the submission package builder uses, so the platform-shaped package is produced from the canonical submission_report_template.md rather than ad-hoc string concatenation.
functional_requirements: Expose load_submission_template(path: str | None = None) -> str that reads the Markdown template from the given path, defaulting to the legacy template at /home/xnihil0zer0/AI-Data/NobleGreed-legacy/orchestrator/templates/submission_report_template.md.
When the resolved template path does not exist or cannot be read, return a built-in default template string that still contains all nine required section headers in order.

Expose render_template(template: str, fields: dict) -> str that replaces named placeholders (e.g. {{title}}, {{cwe}}) with the corresponding field values and substitutes a clear '_Not provided_' marker wherever a referenced field is missing or empty.
spec.interfaces: load_submission_template(path: str | None = None) -> str; render_template(template: str, fields: dict) -> str
edge_cases: Template path points to a missing or permission-denied file.
Template contains placeholders for which no field is supplied.
Fields dict contains keys not referenced by any placeholder (must be ignored, not appended).
non_goals: Do not assemble the full package or map finding/poc/live_report dicts here; that belongs to the builder task.
Do not automate submission to huntr or any bounty platform.
spec.implementation_notes:
